sovereign_country.strategic_role: 极速离岸证券与外汇交易商持牌（VFSC）、轻资产免税出海

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Virtual Private Network and Digital Encryption Software

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Vanuatu International Company (under the International Companies Act, Cap. 222)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (English common law heritage with local statutes; residual customary law and French civil law influences in limited matters)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Vanuatu–Australia Double Taxation Agreement (2016, in force 2017; limited to certain taxes)
Vanuatu–New Zealand Double Taxation Agreement (2016, in force 2018)
Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations (PACER) Plus (signed 2017, provisionally applied; Vanuatu is a Party)

Vanuatu is not a general bilateral investment treaty (BIT) network jurisdiction for substantive investment protection; reliance is placed on domestic International Companies Act, Cap. 222 and Financial Services Authority frameworks

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: International Companies Act, Cap. 222 (Revised Edition 2020); Companies (Amendment) Act No. 21 of 2012; Financial Transactions Reporting Act No. 40 of 2000 (as amended); Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Regulations 2019; Financial Services Authority (FSA) Rule No. 1 of 2020 on the Register of Beneficial Owners; Money Laundering and Proceeds of Crime Act No. 13 of 2002 (as amended); Mutual Assistance in Criminal Matters Act No. 13 of 2004.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (issued post incorporation; for pre-incorporation due diligence, notarized passport and proof of address of proposed director/shareholder are required)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) for certificate; notarization by a licensed notary in the applicant's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Vanuatu acceded to the Apostille Convention on 16 April 2008, effective 1 December 2008) OR Consular Legalization in non-Hague countries

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Certified True Copy of Passport of each proposed director / shareholder / ultimate beneficial owner (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing authority (original); overseas notary public or Vanuatu consular officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent authority of the country of origin OR Consular Legalization by Vanuatu diplomatic mission where the origin country is not a Hague member

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Proof of Residential Address (utility bill or bank statement) dated within 3 months
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or financial institution (original); notarized by a licensed notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter / Professional Reference Letter for each proposed director or shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank or regulated professional (lawyer / accountant) in the applicant's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if issued by a public authority; otherwise notarized and apostilled OR consularized as required by VFSC practice

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of any corporate shareholder/UBO entity (if applicable)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or companies registry of the jurisdiction of incorporation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all proposed directors, shareholders, UBOs, and signatories against Vanuatu Financial Services Authority (VFSC) AML/CFT internal directives, the Vanuatu domestic sanctions list maintained by the Office of the Regulator under the Financial Transactions Reporting Act, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List (as a prudent international correspondent standard), FATF statement and grey/black list indicators, and Interpol notices where reasonably available. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) is mandatory for politically exposed persons (PEPs), family members, and close associates; PEP status is not prohibited but triggers source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, senior management approval, and ongoing transaction monitoring. The registered agent and ultimate beneficial owner register must be maintained at the registered office; any suspicion of money laundering or terrorism financing is reportable to the Vanuatu Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) under the Financial Transactions Reporting Act.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) online name reservation portal (accessible via VFSC's official website vfsc.vu; name reservations are processed through licensed registered agents who submit to VFSC's Companies & International Companies registry)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory requirements: company names must be in Latin script (English or French may be used; Vanuatu is bilingual and the International Companies Act permits English or French names). The name must be distinguishable from existing or reserved names and must not be misleading, deceptive, or contrary to public interest. A transliteration of a name from a non-Latin script into Latin characters is required, and the transliteration must be in accordance with the country of origin's official romanization system (e.g., Pinyin for Chinese names); the reserved name is recorded in the Latin script and any non-Latin script variant may only be ancillary and non-registrable. The name must end with the identifier 'Limited' or the full words 'International Company' or acceptable abbreviated form as prescribed by the Registrar (in practice 'IC' is used as company number suffix, while the registered name is typically 'XXX International Company Limited' or 'XXX Limited').
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Banking, Banker, Trust, Trustee, Insurance, Assurance, Reinsurance, Securities, Exchange, Stockbroker, Fund, Mutual Fund, Superannuation, Credit Union, Deposit, Clearing, Settlement, Financial Services, Money Remittance, Money Service Business, Digital Currency, Crypto, Virtual Asset, Blockchain, VASP (when implying licensable financial activity) — unless licensed by VFSC and the relevant Vanuatu regulatory authority
Visa (if implying payment card network), Mastercard (if implying affiliation), SWIFT, and other trademarks/names suggesting affiliation with payment network operators
International, National, Council, Government, Ministry, Authority, Commission (when implying sovereign or governmental patronage)
Vanuatu (as a standalone token to avoid State affiliation), Port Vila, or any local province name when likely to mislead as to government connection
Names identical or confusingly similar to any existing Vanuatu company, international company, foreign company registered in Vanuatu, or reserved name
Words suggesting a purpose ultra vires the International Company's activities or requiring a local trading licence that the company does not hold
Offensive, obscene, or suggestive tokens contrary to public policy under Cap. 222
Assurance of profit, 'guaranteed returns', 'offshore', 'tax free', 'tax exempt' (when used as part of the name to avoid misrepresentation)
Names containing 'LLC', 'PLLC', 'Ltd and Co' in inconsistent or unauthorized forms not permitted by the International Companies Act
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a name rejection, the applicant (through its licensed registered agent) must file a formal written appeal or re-application to the Registrar of International Companies at the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission setting out the proposed name, the ground of rejection, and the legal and factual basis why the name satisfies Cap. 222 and is distinguishable from existing marks. The appeal must be filed within 14 days of the rejection notice. The Registrar may reconsider and, where competing names are similar, determine on a priority-of-filing basis. If the rejection is based on a prohibited token, the applicant may alternatively apply for ministerial or VFSC waiver consent by demonstrating the intended business is properly licensed or the token is not misleading; any waiver must be evidenced in writing. If the Registrar upholds the rejection, the applicant may seek judicial review in the Supreme Court of Vanuatu under the Rules of the Supreme Court (Judicial Review) within 30 days. Extension of a successful name reservation may be requested before the expiry of the initial 30-day window, at the Registrar's discretion and for good cause shown, but each extension is normally limited to a further 30 days and an additional statutory fee is payable.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are generally permissible for the e-commerce/VPN SaaS business model, provided that a physical registered office in Vanuatu is maintained at all times through a licensed registered agent. The registered agent's street address in Vanuatu is the registered office and is the legal service of process address. The company's actual operational decision-making and core income-generating activities may be conducted remotely; however, if the VPN/network security business derives income through a Vanuatu permanent establishment or conducts Vanuatu-sourced activities, the substance requirements under the Income Tax Act Cap. 142 (as amended) and the International Companies Act must be reviewed. A pure foreign-sourced income international company will not require local staff or premises, provided no virtual office is held out as a substantive management location in Vanuatu. The virtual office provider may not be the same as the registered agent unless the provider itself is a licensed registered agent.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk of unannounced physical on-site inspections: 2%–3% per year for a low-profile e-commerce / VPN subscription business held-out as an International Company with no local employees and no local revenue, but the risk escalates to 12%–18% if the company uses a local virtual office address on its website or payment pages, applies for a Vanuatu VAT registration, or is flagged by the FIU for unusual transaction volumes by non-resident clients. VFSC and the registered agent are entitled without notice to inspect the registered office for statutory records (share register, beneficial ownership register, and accounting records); failure to maintain records invites penalties.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under VFSC fees schedule (International Companies Regulations Cap. 222)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO register establishment and initial BO declaration (first year)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Registered agent compliance fee plus VFSC regulatory filing fee under FSA Rule 1 of 2020

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing professional hourly rate (fixed fee) for offshore tax advisory opinion

incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) — International Companies Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation of an International Company (Form 1/IC), together with Memorandum and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital; the Company may adopt nominal share capital (commonly USD 1) denominated in any approved currency, and there is no escrow or capital-deposit requirement under the International Companies Act 1992.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that, upon registration, the Company accept the subscriber’s subscription for Ordinary Shares at a nominal value of USD 1 per share and that such shares be issued and recorded in the register of members. RESOLVED FURTHER that the registered office of the Company be established at the address of the licensed registered agent in Port Vila, Vanuatu, and that the registered agent be retained. RESOLVED FURTHER that the persons named in the accompanying consent forms be and are hereby appointed as first directors and secretary to hold office under the International Companies Act 1992. RESOLVED FURTHER that the directors be authorized to open bank accounts, appoint service providers, and execute contracts necessary to commence operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) — Online Companies Registry Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name search and reservation application through the VFSC portal or by written application to the Registry. Provide the proposed company name, purpose clause, and registered agent consent. The Registry will issue a name-reservation certificate if the name is distinguishable and not prohibited under the International Companies Act 1992.
required_dossiers: Certified passport copies of ultimate beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for conflict, obscenity, or similarity, file a written request for reconsideration or submit up to three alternative names within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered Agent in Vanuatu and Offshore Notary / Licensing Practitioner
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the licensed registered agent to draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in compliance with the International Companies Act 1992. Have the incorporator or subscriber sign the documents before a notary public, compelling the agent to certify the signatures and retain originals for filing.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as director (two directors)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If constitutional documents are queried for inconsistency, file amended articles and a rectification affidavit with the VFSC within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Application and Payment of Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission — Companies Registration Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the completed Form 1/IC together with the Memorandum, Articles, registered agent consent, and declaration of compliance. Pay the prescribed incorporation and annual maintenance fees by bank transfer to the VFSC designated account. The Registry will issue a Certificate of Incorporation upon approval.
required_dossiers: Certified true copy of memorandum and articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a query notice, provide supplementary declarations or corrected documentation within seven business days; failure to cure may result in withdrawal and refund less administrative fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Corporate Governance and Statutory Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation, convene the first board of directors meeting and adopt the pro-forma board resolution. Issue share certificates, open the register of members, register of directors, register of secretaries, and minute book. File any changes of particulars with the VFSC through the registered agent.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If statutory records are challenged during audit or a later filing, reconstruct the registers under director’s declaration and re-file with the VFSC with a late-filing explanation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Licence and Physical Premises Clearance (if Local Operations)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Industry and Municipal Council Licensing Office (Port Vila)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the International Company maintains a physical office, server room, or local hiring, apply for a Business Licence under the Business Licence Act and obtain municipal zoning consent. For a purely offshore VPN/SaaS operation with no Vanuatu physical establishment, obtain a Certificate of Non-Residence / No Physical Presence from the registered agent and retain it with the corporate records.
required_dossiers: Labour and workplace certificate (if employees in Vanuatu)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If licensing is contested due to physical-presence determination, submit an operational affidavit and an inspection report; if the municipality requires conditions, apply for a conditional business licence within five business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Vanuatu Department of Industry, Ministry of Trade, Tourism, Industry and Investment
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Licence (ICT / Digital Services) issued under the Business Licence Act [Cap. 252] — Class 2 Information and Communication Services

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Vanuatu Department of Environmental Protection, Ministry of Climate Change and Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Registration Category 2 — no full EIA report is required for a VPN and digital encryption software SaaS operation with no physical industrial plant; a simple environmental registration is sufficient if the company operates any office facility.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or point-source VOC emissions thresholds apply to intangible VPN software services; any office waste must be managed in accordance with the Vanuatu Waste Management Act 2003 and discharge limits under the Water Resources Management Act if sanitary effluent enters public sewers.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate issued by Vanuatu Fire and Emergency Services; structural and occupancy inspection by the Public Works Department; electrical installation certificate from the licensed electrician; and workplace registration/occupational health clearance from the Department of Labour.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Vanuatu Revenue and Customs Authority (VRCA), Port Vila; official portal: https://vrca.gov.vu (VAT registration and TIN services administered under the Value Added Tax Act No. 3 of 1998 and the Tax Administration (Penalties) Act)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned International Company (IC) obtains a statutory TIN/VAT ID by applying to the VRCA on the prescribed VAT registration form, accompanied by the certificate of incorporation under the International Companies Act Cap. 222, the registered agent details, director identity documents, and proof of the registered office in Vanuatu. VAT registration is compulsory within 21 days after the taxable turnover of the IC supplier reaches or exceeds VT 10,000,000 in any consecutive 12-month period; voluntary registration is available below the threshold. The IC is assigned a 9-digit VAT registration number and, where applicable, payroll/income tax accounts are not required because the IC is tax-exempt.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch elections are available under Vanuatu law. The International Company enjoys a statutory 20-year exemption from all Vanuatu income, corporate, capital gains, withholding, and stamp taxes under the International Companies Act Cap. 222, renewable for further 20-year periods upon re-registration. The IC may elect to remain entirely outside the domestic VAT net by restricting all supplies to non-resident customers of offshore-network services, and no optional VAT grouping or special fiscal-regime election is provided.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Value Added Tax Act No. 3 of 1998, as amended
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: VT 10,000,000 (ten million vatu) of taxable supplies in any consecutive 12-month period; mandatory VRCA registration within 21 days of exceeding the threshold, with voluntary registration permitted below it
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time electronic-invoicing clearance, fiscal API, or digital stamping mandate exists in Vanuatu. Taxable suppliers may issue manual or printed VAT invoices and must retain all books, invoices, and records for a minimum of 7 years; the VRCA relies on post-audit invoice verification and bank-record cross-checks rather than transaction-level digital clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating at 0% applies under the VAT Act where (i) goods are exported by the supplier in the course or furtherance of a taxable activity, or (ii) services are supplied to a non-resident customer and are physically performed entirely outside Vanuatu. For the VPN Network Privacy App SaaS, the IC must establish that the digital service is rendered to non-resident subscribers, the servers/usage occur outside Vanuatu, and the consideration is received in foreign currency and attributable to offshore supplies; services merely consumed incidentally in Vanuatu or supplied to Vanuatu residents are excluded from zero-rating and remain taxable at 15%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (outward manifest / export entry form filed with the Vanuatu Customs Division)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical export movement of any associated hardware/media
Commercial Invoice describing the VPN service and confirming the non-resident recipient
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank/Stripe-Paymentwall settlement statement evidencing receipt of export proceeds
Non-resident Customer Declaration and IP/usage-location log demonstrating offshore consumption of the digital service
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Vanuatu imposes no exchange-control repatriation deadline for IC export proceeds because the IC operates wholly in foreign currency and is outside the domestic tax net; nonetheless, the VRCA may disregard zero-rating where export evidence is deficient. Fraudulent or unsupported zero-rating claims trigger reassessment at 15% VAT on the full supply value, additional tax up to 25% of the unpaid VAT for late payment, a 100% civil penalty on the tax shortfall for deliberate misdeclaration, and retrospective clawback of any input credits, plus interest accruing from the original due date. Knowingly submitting false declarations, forged export documentation, or wilfully obstructing the VRCA is a criminal offence punishable by fines up to VT 500,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years, with directors and the registered agent jointly and severally liable in the case of an International Company.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of Vanuatu (RBV) — established under the Reserve Bank of Vanuatu Act [Cap. 125]; statutory monetary authority for the Vanuatu Vatu (VUV), regulator of licensed financial institutions and authorized foreign exchange dealers, and operator of the Vanuatu Clearing System.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: VUV is fully convertible on both current and capital account; Vanuatu has no exchange control legislation, no capital-movement approval mechanism, and no restriction on profit, dividend, or capital repatriation. An International Company (IC) incorporated under the International Companies Act [Cap. 222] is expressly exempt from exchange control requirements and may freely transfer funds in and out of the jurisdiction. Practical remittance friction is limited to commercial AML/KYC screening by correspondents, not regulatory approval; there is no black-market premium, no surrender obligation, no approval for inward foreign direct investment, and no repatriation timeline. The de facto settlement currency for the VPN SaaS business is USD, with VUV conversion available at authorized-dealer interbank rates.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Vanuatu imposes no mandatory surrender of export or service-rendering proceeds, no holding-period requirement, and no forced conversion ratio for export receipts. The RBV prescribes no statutory timeline for disposition of foreign currency earnings; VPN SaaS export receivables may be retained indefinitely in USD or converted at the prevailing authorized-dealer rate.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Multi-Currency Account (USD/AUD/VUV) for SaaS collections and treasury
Operational Corporate Current Account (VUV/USD/AUD) for trade settlement and disbursements
Operational Corporate Account and Foreign Currency Account (USD/VUV), incl. ATM/EFTPOS and online banking
Operational Account (primarily VUV; limited foreign-currency capability and conservative offshore-IC acceptance)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low direct viability. Leading digital EMIs and neo-banks (Stripe Treasury, Wise Business, Airwallex, Currenxie, Mercury) either do not support Vanuatu-incorporated entities or apply hard jurisdiction blocks due to Vanuatu's prior FATF grey-listing remediation status, the offshore IC structure, and the VPN/privacy industry's Medium-Risk-Enhanced profile. Feasible architecture: (1) open a Tier-1 Vanuatu bank account (ANZ/BSP/BRED) as the primary settlement account; (2) aggregate Stripe and Paymentwall payouts into the Vanuatu account via SWIFT MT103; (3) use the IC's VFSC-registered agent and substance documentation to satisfy any second-tier EMI application, assessing each provider's country list individually before commitment. Direct reliance on a single offshore EMI as the primary treasury channel is not legally or operationally defensible.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is practically mandated for all International Company onboarding at ANZ, BSP, BRED, and NBV. At least one director or duly authorized signatory must attend an in-person interview at a Port Vila branch, presenting original certified corporate documents (Certificate of Incorporation, Memorandum and Articles, register of directors and members), valid passport, proof of residential address, and a board resolution authorizing account opening and signatories. Remote opening is not formally permitted for non-resident, 100%-foreign-owned ICs; video KYC may supplement but cannot substitute for the in-person interview. This mandate reflects the RBV's enhanced AML/CFT enforcement posture following Vanuatu's FATF grey-list remediation action plan.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore International Company with non-resident ownership, no local economic footprint, and potential bearer-share or nominee-shareholder history
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the IC Registration Certificate under Cap. 222; current Register of Members and Register of Directors naming all natural-person UBOs and their % holding; notarized UBO declaration and trust/ownership chart if layered; VFSC-licensed registered agent's compliance letter confirming beneficial-ownership filing with the Vanuatu Beneficial Ownership Registry; board resolution identifying account purpose, expected transaction profile, and authorized signatories; source-of-wealth statement and bank references of each UBO; explanation of operational substance (VPN server agreements, subcontractors, end-customer geography).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Industry risk: VPN network and digital privacy application associated with anonymization tools, circumvention of censorship, potential illicit-use exposure, and elevated TF exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Regulatory opinion confirming the service is lawful encryption/conduit software (ISIC 6201 / NAICS 517919) and that no VFSC financial-services license is triggered; customer anti-abuse and acceptable-use policy; IP geolocation, device fingerprinting, and bot-detection tooling; geo-blocking of sanctioned jurisdictions; no cryptocurrency, mixing, or money-laundering functionality within the product; privacy framework (GDPR-aligned data processing, ISO 27001 gap assessment); sample subscription agreement with corporate/non-anonymous consumer terms; monthly OFAC/UN/EU sanctions and negative-news screening reports; identification of hosting providers and subprocessors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency third-party settlement inflows from Stripe and Paymentwall, presenting commingling, card-chargeback, and unvouchered receivables risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Processor payout reports (Stripe, Paymentwall) matching gross/net subscription revenue to bank MT103 credits; 12-month historical statements from the UBO's home jurisdiction or prior corporate bank; a listing of expected settlement days and volume bands; board-approved debit-memo protocol; customer invoicing/sales ledger; reconciliation procedure and chart-of-accounts mapping; evidence that payment processors themselves conduct merchant KYC/KYB; chargeback and refund policy documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions exposure from VPN customer traffic originating in or terminating to high-risk jurisdictions (e.g., Russia, Iran, or UN/OFAC-listed territories)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions-screening policy embedded at onboarding and continuously applied to subscriber IP and payment card BINs; geo-blocking configuration evidence from the VPN platform; monthly OFAC/UN/EU/UK sanctions-list audit reports; attestation of no sanctioned-country sales; data-flow diagram showing infrastructure in approved jurisdictions (e.g., Singapore, Germany, Netherlands, United States); FIU/RBV audit trail demonstrating remediation of any flagged transaction; log-retention and subpoena-response policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Zero-tax IC status, audit exemption, and perceived absence of commercial substance triggering bank reputational concern
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: VFSC tax-exemption certificate under Cap. 222; statutory audit-exemption confirmation from a Vanuatu-licensed chartered accountant; voluntary preparation of IFRS-compliant financial statements to provide bank comfort; transfer-pricing policy and intercompany agreements if fees flow to related infrastructure entities; bank-native finance questionnaire demonstrating real revenue, real expenses (hosting, legal, accounting, registered agent), and realistic liquidity needs; undertaking to provide quarterly management accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payments to low-tax and cloud-service counterparties that resemble profit-stripping or undisclosed lending
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully executed hosting/CDN/software license agreements with invoices and evidence of service delivery (dashboards, bandwidth usage reports); SWIFT MT103 remittance schedules with exact commercial purpose codes and narratives; intercompany loan agreements with arm's-length interest and repayment schedule, if any; advance pricing arrangement documentation; board minutes authorizing the vendor scheme; registered agent annual-continuation and maintenance records.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: (1) shareholders' capital contribution resolution and board minutes authorizing the injection; (2) remitting bank executes SWIFT MT103 with purpose code referencing 'equity injection into International Company' (BPM6 category 5M2 - equity capital); (3) beneficiary line must exactly match the IC legal name and the Tier-1 Vanuatu account number; (4) reference field carries the share-allotment serial number; (5) remitter's bank must be the UBO's actual bank, with 6 months of account statements attached to the KYC file; (6) no exchange-control permit is required because Vanuatu imposes no inward-remittance approval; (7) if the remittance is characterized as shareholder loan rather than equity, a signed loan agreement, interest-rate policy, and intercompany documentation must be retained to prevent FIU mischaracterization; (8) funds settle in USD or VUV via SWIFT correspondent, typically T+1–T+2 from Australia or Singapore.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rail: SWIFT MT103 for operating disbursements (cloud hosting, CDN bandwidth, software licenses, legal, accounting, registered-agent fees, director costs) with field 70 (Remittance Information) containing a precise commercial invoice reference; no outward exchange-control permit required. For high-value infrastructure procurement exceeding USD 250,000, a sight or usance Commercial Letter of Credit can be arranged through ANZ or BSP, though availability is limited and typically requires 50–100% cash margin from an IC with no track record; confirm whether the beneficiary accepts documentary collections. Local VUV clearing runs through the RBV-operated Vanuatu Clearing System on a T+1 basis; cross-border clearing uses SWIFT correspondents in Australia (AUD), New Zealand (NZD), Singapore (USD), and Europe (EUR). Reconciliations are reinforced by MT940/MT942 statements; payment disputes are traced via MT195/MT199 and reversed via MT192/MT292.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright spot and forward contracts in VUV/USD, VUV/AUD, and VUV/NZD (tenors up to 12 months) through authorized dealers (ANZ, BSP, BRED) — permissible without RBV approval because VUV is fully convertible and no corporate derivative-licensing regime applies

Cross-currency swaps (USD/VUV and AUD/VUV) — legally permissible for hedging subscription revenue timing mismatches; market-making is narrow and banks quote bilaterally with credit support/collateral for tenors of 3–12 months
Multi-currency account netting and natural hedging — matching USD receivables from Stripe/Paymentwall against USD payables to hosting/CDN providers to eliminate excessive VUV conversion

Plain-vanilla interest-rate or currency swaps written with a licensed Vanuatu bank as end-user hedge — permissible provided the swap relates to genuine commercial exposure and is documented under an ISDA Credit Support Annex

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) on VUV — legally unnecessary and commercially impractical because VUV is not a restricted or inconvertible currency requiring NDF treatment; reliance on deliverable forwards and natural hedging is the preferred compliance posture

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return and annual government maintenance fee payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) - International Companies Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one calendar month of the anniversary of incorporation each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of VUV 2,500 per month or part thereof; continued default beyond the VFSC notice period may result in administrative strike-off and loss of separate legal personality.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Economic Substance Notification / Nil economic substance return for non-relevant activities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 12 months of the entity's financial year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may trigger penalties under the Vanuatu Economic Substance Regulations, including fines up to VUV 1,000,000 and potential strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent Annual Compliance Confirmation and UBO verification update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC), administered by the licensed registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At the date of the annual return filing each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: AML/CFT breach penalties, including fines up to VUV 10,000,000 and revocation of the agent's license; UBO information must be current and verifiable.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit only if the International Company holds a financial services license (banking, insurance, securities, or fiduciary), or if shareholders holding at least 10% of voting shares require an audit. A VPN network and privacy software company with no statutory license is audit-exempt unless such requirement is voluntarily imposed.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or materially equivalent local GAAP may be used; the International Companies Act requires financial records sufficient to show and explain transactions with reasonable accuracy, but no audited financial statements must be filed for a non-licensee exempt entity.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The registered agent must identify and verify all beneficial owners owning or controlling more than 25% of shares or voting rights and confirm the UBO schedule at each annual return filing. Any share transfer or change of control must be notified to the registered agent within 14 days; there is no public UBO register in Vanuatu, but the agent is statutorily obliged to retain and update the information confidentially for law enforcement access.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - USD 5,000 if voluntarily appointed or required by a shareholder resolution

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Vanuatu International Companies are wholly exempt from corporate income tax, capital gains tax, and any branch or dividend withholding tax. There are no tax holidays; the 0% rate is inherent in the International Companies Act, and no domestic VAT/GST, payroll tax, or social security levy applies to the VPN software SaaS business.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: None (no CIT return). The only recurring statutory filing is the International Company Annual Return, submitted by the registered agent to the VFSC / Registrar of International Companies (VFSC electronic portal used by licensed agents).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 30 days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation; no fiscal-year-end correspondence due to the absence of an income tax regime.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the International Company and its unique VU IC registry number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the exact English name in capital letters; no tax registration ID is required or available.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name and Vanuatu address of the licensed registered agent and office.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: An International Company must maintain a registered agent in Vanuatu; the overseas owner cannot self-file or sign this annual return without the agent's countersignature.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Residential addresses and identification data of all directors and the secretary.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Directors may be non-residents; provide passport, proof of address, and beneficial-owner declaration to the registered agent for AML filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Number of issued shares, class details, and controlling beneficial owner declaration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All shares may be held by a non-resident; the beneficial-owner schedule is mandatory for AML/CFT compliance even though the entity is tax-exempt.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or non-filing of the annual return triggers VFSC late-payment fees, automatic late penalty where applicable, and can lead to the deregistration/strike-off of the International Company. Once struck off, assets vest in the Vanuatu Government and restoration requires court or Registrar-sanctioned procedures with substantial penalties.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Not applicable. Vanuatu has no comprehensive double taxation agreements and therefore no treaty relief process, TRC submission, or reduced rate protocol. Dividends are paid freely by resolution without any withholding, and no exchange control approval is required for non-resident shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 0% statutory rate. As no tax treaty network exists, the 0% domestic rate is the effective rate on cross-border royalties, software licence fees, and interest paid to foreign related parties.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: None prescribed. Vanuatu has not enacted transfer pricing legislation or Local File/Master File thresholds. A prudent VPN group should nonetheless maintain contemporaneous intercompany pricing documentation and a transfer pricing report if cross-border controlled transactions exceed VUV 100,000,000 to defend against foreign taxes and substance audits.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Vanuatu's economic substance requirements apply to International Companies carrying on relevant activities, including intellectual property holding, distribution and service centres, and financing. A VPN/network security SaaS company deriving revenue from software licensing or global subscriptions must show Vanuatu-based direction and control, staff, premises, and adequate operating expenditure; otherwise the tax-exempt status can be challenged, and the company may face annual ESR filing and penalty obligations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion via Sham Offshore Structure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the zero-tax International Company as a mere collection vehicle for VPN subscriptions while all strategic decision-making and actual software development occur outside Vanuatu, with no local substance and with revenue concealed from the foreign beneficial owner's tax administration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fraudulent use of an International Company is sanctionable under the International Companies Act and general criminal law; penalties may include strike-off, disqualification of the registered agent, a fine up to VT 10 million, and/or up to two years' imprisonment; in cross-border cases, the underlying foreign tax offense remains separately prosecutable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil may be pierced where the company is a façade. Directors and beneficial owners can be ordered to make civil restitution of diverted profits, are subject to travel bans while under investigation, and may serve imprisonment for tax fraud in jurisdictions receiving Vanuatu's mutual legal assistance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: IC files annual returns but exists solely as a letterbox with nominee directors, no physical office, no independent staff, and no decision-making in Vanuatu while licensing valuable IP to related entities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Vanuatu ESR regime imposes specific penalties for failure to file substance declarations or for false declarations, including monetary penalties of up to VT 5 million per annum, forced dissolution of the International Company, and referral to the Financial Intelligence Unit if evasion is suspected.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a shell entity are individually liable for knowing participation in false ESR filings; courts may disallow the exemption, hold directors personally liable for debts incurred with no genuine business, and ban them from acting as directors in Vanuatu for up to 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing VPN subscription payments through Stripe or Paymentwall while deliberately concealing sanctioned-country customers, using renamed merchant accounts, or failing to disclose the ultimate beneficial owner to the registered agent or payment processor.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Vanuatu Anti-Money Laundering and Counter Financing of Terrorism Act, non-compliance with CDD, record-keeping, and suspicious transaction reporting is a criminal offence subject to fines applicable to the company and imprisonment for compliance officers; the Proceeds of Crime Act permits freezing and confiscation of assets gained from unlawful conduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly participate in sanctions evasion or money laundering face personal criminal prosecution, financial penalties, travel restrictions, and confiscation of personal assets; beneficial owners may also be subjected to foreign OFAC/EU equivalent listings, triggering VFSC de-registration.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Fraud / Artificial Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A related foreign developer licenses software code or trademarks to the Vanuatu IC under inflated royalties to shift profits into the zero-tax entity, while the Vanuatu IC lacks employees, office, or substantive functions supporting the IP licence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: No direct domestic Vanuatu transfer pricing penalty applies because there is no income tax; however, the sham transaction can trigger foreign anti-avoidance legislation, withholding tax reassessments, and severe penalties equal to 20% to 40% of adjusted profits in the counterparty jurisdiction, plus interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foreign revenue courts may pierce the veil of the Vanuatu IC and impose joint civil liability on directors for the hidden tax, along with personal payment orders, contempt-of-court sanctions, and the risk of international arrest where intentional fraud is established.
